Combined with the earlier (2.4.0) warning when the legacy keyring is used and the 2.9.24 deprecation of trusted.gpg.d for sources without Signed-By, third-party keys installed only into /etc/apt/trusted.gpg are silently ignored at verify time. The symptom is `The repository ... is not signed` / `NO_PUBKEY <KEYID>` during `apt-get update` for repos whose key was historically added by `apt-key add` (which wrote to trusted.gpg).

actions.hint: Move each third-party key into its own keyring under /etc/apt/keyrings/ and reference it from the source entry: `deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/<name>.gpg] https://...`. For deb822 .sources files use the `Signed-By:` field.

As an interim, you can re-arm trusted.gpg.d (still read in this release) by dropping a single binary keyring there: `gpg --no-default-keyring --keyring /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/<name>.gpg --import <key.asc>`. Avoid /etc/apt/trusted.gpg itself.
Pin apt to a version < 2.9.24 (Debian bookworm or earlier) where the trusted.gpg fallback still works while the source list is migrated.

non_solutions: Re-exporting the key with gpg and re-running apt-key add has no effect; apt-key is gone (2.9.17) and trusted.gpg is unread (2.9.24).
Setting Acquire::AllowInsecureRepositories "true"; works around verification but is unsafe and lintian-forbidden.

summary: apt 2.9.11 deleted the ftp, rsh and ssh transport methods (disabled-by-default since apt 1.8); sources.list entries using ftp://, rsh:// or ssh:// now fail to fetch.
mechanism: The ftp/rsh/ssh acquire methods were disabled in apt 1.8 and physically removed from the apt source tree in 2.9.11 ("Remove ftp, rsh, ssh methods (disabled since 1.8)"). `apt update` against a `deb ftp://mirror...` line now reports an unsupported transport, breaking legacy mirror setups, air-gapped build hosts that pulled packages over rsh/ssh tunnels, and Debian stretch-era FTP-only mirror configurations. Debian-hosted mirrors also shut down FTP access at the stretch release (release-notes 5.1.2 "FTP access to Debian hosted mirrors will be removed").
trigger_patterns: The method driver /usr/lib/apt/methods/ftp could not be found.
The method driver /usr/lib/apt/methods/rsh could not be found.
The method driver /usr/lib/apt/methods/ssh could not be found.

actions.hint: Rewrite every `deb ftp://host/path` (or rsh://, ssh://) entry to https:// or http://. For private mirrors that genuinely need SSH, use the sshfs/fuse mount or rsync; for read-only local mirrors use `deb file:/path/...`.
For Debian stretch-era setups the release-notes already document the migration: `deb http://deb.debian.org/debian <suite> main` and `deb http://deb.debian.org/debian-security <suite>/updates main`.
If you cannot edit the sources, use an older Debian release (apt < 1.8 still ships the methods) just for the apt update step.

non_solutions: Installing apt-transport-ftp does not exist; no separate transport package is provided.
Adding Acquire::ftp::Proxy configuration does not resurrect the deleted method.

summary: apt 2.9.2 changed diagnostic line prefixes from E:/W:/N: to Error:/Warning:/Notice: (and re-rendered them in bold/color); build scripts and CI that grep ^E: to detect apt errors now miss failures.
mechanism: apt 2.9.2 changelog (i18n: "Use Error:/Warning:/Notice: instead of E:/W:/N:") rewrote the per-message severity prefix and made the whole message bold. Tools that scrape apt output by matching `^E:`, `^W:`, `^N:` (a very common pattern in CI dashboards, build scripts, and Debian packaging wrappers) stop seeing new errors. The behavioral effect is that a build pipeline can silently miss a genuine apt-get failure (e.g. during `apt build-dep`), continue, and only fail later with a confusing compile/link error.apt 2.9.2 also added --color / --no-color and the APT_NO_COLOR variable, so the bold/color rendering is another trap for naive grep on stderr.

actions.hint: Update any `grep -E "^E:|^W:"` style detection to `(E|Error):` / `(W|Warning):` / `(N|Notice):`, or simply rely on apt exit codes which are unchanged.
Set APT_NO_COLOR=1 (or pass --no-color, available since 2.9.2) before scraping output; colour escape codes would also break naive grep on the new prefix.
To keep the legacy prefix for tooling that cannot be changed, downgrade the apt package to < 2.9.2 in a build container.

non_solutions: Just grepping for "Error" without anchoring the prefix matches unrelated package descriptions and changelog text.

summary: apt 2.9.26 introduced `apt modernize-sources`, deprecated the legacy one-line .list format (removal not before 2029), and nags about .list sources lacking a Signed-By=, confusing CI logs.
mechanism: Starting with apt 2.9.26 the one-line-style format used in /etc/apt/sources.list and *.list under sources.list.d is officially deprecated; apt prints a notice (W: in older format, Notice: under 2.9.2+) on every `apt update` if any .list source lacks an explicit `signed-by=`. Trixie release notes 4.3 / 4.7 tell users to convert to the deb822 .sources format with a Signed-By: field. apt 2.9.26 changelog: "Deprecate legacy one-line-style format harder. Removal not before 2029." and "Set signed-by/Signed-By in sources.list(5) short examples". The notice is benign but can scroll off real errors and trip strict CI that fails on stderr.

actions.hint: Run `apt modernize-sources` (introduced in 2.9.26) on the build host; it converts each .list to a deb822 .sources file, sets Signed-By: where possible, and disables the old .list.

Hand-convert a one-line entry to deb822, e.g. `deb [arch=amd64 signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/example.gpg] https://example.com stable main` becomes a debian.sources stanza with Types: deb / URIs: https://example.com / Suites: stable / Components: main / Signed-By: /etc/apt/keyrings/example.gpg.
Suppress the notice in non-interactive build scripts by running with `-o APT::Color="false"` and quiet mode `apt-get update -qq`; the warning itself is advisory.

non_solutions: Switching to deb822 without a Signed-By field keeps the notice; Signed-By must be set explicitly.

summary: apt 3.1.10 enables the new 3.0 (solver3) dependency solver by default; resolution differs and dependency-conflict messages are reformatted, breaking fragile `apt build-dep`/`apt-get install` heuristics.
mechanism: apt 3.1.10 changelog: "Enable the new solver by default in 0.31, 1.21, 2.11, 3.1" via per-suite CLI version tables. The 3.0 solver (work began in 2.9.29 "Major 3.0 solver update") produces different upgrade/install plans than the legacy/edsp solver, and 2.9.32 "Produce more human-readable dependency errors in 3.0 solver" reformatted dependency errors. `apt build-dep <pkg>` against an OLD source can therefore pick different -dev packages or refuse an installation that previously worked, and CI logs that pattern-match old "but it is not going to be installed" strings break.
trigger_patterns: but it is not going to be installed
negative_patterns: E: Could not perform immediate configuration

actions.hint: Invoke the legacy solver when provisioning build dependencies: call `apt --solver internal build-dep <pkg>` (or `apt-get --solver internal install <pkgs>`). The --solver option has existed since apt 2.4.0 ("Allow --solver apt to work on apt satisfy"); `internal` selects the legacy edsp solver while `3.0`/`solver3` is the new solver enabled by default for recorded cli-versions {0.31, 1.21, 2.11, 3.1} (3.1.10).

Pin to Debian bookworm (apt 2.6.x) for build-dependency provisioning while the new-solver plan is investigated; bookworm's recorded cli-version is not in the solver3-default set, so it still resolves to the legacy internal solver.

non_solutions: Downgrading only apt does not change behaviour if the recorded cli-version still resolves to solver3; you must explicitly request the internal solver.

summary: Debian 11 (bullseye) is the LAST release to ship apt-key; the release notes explicitly tell users to migrate keys to /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/*.gpg|*.asc, and bookworm+ no longer works as before.
mechanism: Bullseye release notes 5.3.2 "Deprecated components for bullseye" states verbatim: "bullseye is the final Debian release to ship apt-key. Keys should be managed by dropping files into /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d instead, in binary format as created by gpg --export with a .gpg extension, or ASCII armored with a .asc extension." On bullseye itself apt-key still works, but build scripts that target multiple Debian releases must not rely on it from bookworm onward, and the deprecated-components notice is printed during dist-upgrade.
trigger_patterns: bullseye is the final Debian release to ship apt-key
Keys should be managed by dropping files into /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d

actions.hint: Migrate setup scripts now: replace `curl <url> | apt-key add -` with `install -m0755 -d /etc/apt/keyrings && curl -fsSL <url> | gpg --dearmor -o /etc/apt/keyrings/<name>.gpg` and set signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/<name>.gpg on the deb line.
For builds that still need apt-key, target bullseye (apt 2.2.x) explicitly until the migration is complete.

non_solutions: Continuing to call apt-key "because it still works on bullseye" — it will fail on bookworm+ and is already unsupported.

summary: apt (dist|full)-upgrade aborts with `E: Could not perform immediate configuration on '<pkg>'` during dependency loops; documented for every release from wheezy through trixie.
mechanism: Release notes from wheezy (4.5.1) through trixie (4.5.1) document: "In some cases the apt[-get] (dist|full)-upgrade step can fail after downloading packages with: `E: Could not perform immediate configuration on 'package'. Please see man 5 apt.conf under APT::Immediate-Configure for details.`" apt refuses to unpack/configure a package whose dependencies cannot be immediately configured, which is common when an OLD build environment is being dist-upgraded in place (libc6/gcc/libstdc++ transitions, dependency loops with Pre-Depends). The build then cannot proceed to compile anything until the loop is resolved.
trigger_patterns: E: Could not perform immediate configuration on '
Could not perform immediate configuration on '

actions.hint: Run `apt full-upgrade -o APT::Immediate-Configure=0` (or `apt-get dist-upgrade -o APT::Immediate-Configure=0` on older releases) to disable the immediate-configure check and let dpkg configure everything at the end. The release-notes section is the canonical source for this workaround.
Temporarily add BOTH the old and the new suite (e.g. bullseye and bookworm) to your sources.list, run `apt update`, then retry the full-upgrade; once the upgrade is complete, drop the old-suite line.
If the loop is fundamental (e.g. mixing unstable+stable pins), provision a clean container with only the target suite and rebuild the build-dependency set there rather than dist-upgrading in place.

non_solutions: Forcing `apt-get -f install` does not resolve the loop; the error is a solver policy, not a broken state.
Switching to aptitude does not always help; aptitude uses its own resolver and the immediate-configure policy is the same.

summary: Upgrading an OLD squeeze system that installed ia32-libs to wheezy fails with `ia32-libs : Depends: ia32-libs-i386 but it is not installable / E: Broken packages` unless i386 multiarch is enabled first.
mechanism: Wheezy release notes 4.5.2 "Transitioning from ia32-libs to multiarch" document verbatim: "Debian 7.0 now features multiarch ... The ia32-libs package is now a transitional package to make use of this new functionality. If you have ia32-libs installed, you need to enable multiarch before upgrading this package. Otherwise APT will output the following message: `The following packages have unmet dependencies: ia32-libs : Depends: ia32-libs-i386 but it is not installable / E: Broken packages`." If `dpkg --add-architecture i386` has not been run, apt cannot see any :i386 packages and refuses the upgrade. This blocks the upgrade path and any subsequent `apt build-dep` for cross-32-bit C/C++ projects.
trigger_patterns: ia32-libs : Depends: ia32-libs-i386 but it is not installable
ia32-libs-i386 but it is not installable
The following packages have unmet dependencies:
negative_patterns: E: Could not perform immediate configuration
E: Unable to locate package ia32-libs

actions.hint: Enable the i386 architecture before the upgrade: `dpkg --add-architecture i386` then `apt-get update`. After that the transitional ia32-libs can be resolved, or replaced by the actual :i386 packages (libfoo:i386).
Skip the transitional entirely: stay on squeeze for the build, or move directly to a non-multiarch 32-bit chroot.

non_solutions: Installing ia32-libs-i386 by hand does not work; multiarch must be enabled first.
Force-installing the .deb with dpkg -i leaves apt in a broken state.

summary: Multiarch (wheezy) moved system libraries to /usr/lib/<triplet>/, breaking hard-coded /usr/lib and /lib paths in legacy configure.ac / CMakeLists / Makefiles that grep the filesystem instead of asking the toolchain.
mechanism: Wheezy release notes 5.13 "Multiarch implications for the toolchain" warn verbatim: "The introduction of multiarch changes the paths for some files, which may break assumptions made by toolchain components. Debian's toolchain has been updated, but users trying to build or use external compilers might need to be aware of this." Concrete effect: glibc/gcc now install libraries under triplet-suffixed paths (e.g. /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so instead of /usr/lib/libc.so). An OLD project's configure.ac / CMakeLists.txt that does `ls /usr/lib/libfoo.so` or hard-codes `-L/usr/lib` fails to find libraries at configure time, so the build aborts before any C/C++ compilation starts. The release notes also reference /usr/share/doc/libc6/NEWS.Debian.gz and Debian bug #637232.
trigger_patterns: file not recognized: file format not recognized
can not be used when making a shared object

actions.hint: Derive the multiarch libdir from the toolchain rather than hard-coding /usr/lib: pass `pkg-config --libs-only-L <pkg>` or `gcc -print-search-dirs | grep install`; for CMake set `-DCMAKE_LIBRARY_ARCHITECTURE=$(dpkg-architecture -qDEB_HOST_MULTIARCH)`.

In configure.ac use AC_CHECK_LIB([foo], [bar]) (which uses the compiler, not the filesystem) instead of `test -f /usr/lib/libfoo.so`. In CMakeLists use find_package(foo) / pkg_check_modules(foo REQUIRED foo) rather than find_path(... /usr/lib).
Build on a pre-wheezy (squeeze) toolchain container if the project cannot be edited; this avoids the multiarch path layout entirely.

non_solutions: Symlinking /usr/lib/<triplet>/* into /usr/lib is fragile, unsupported, and breaks on dpkg --search.
Editing the compiled C/C++ source does not help; the failure is at configure/link time and is path-related.

summary: Debian stretch (9) shut down FTP access to Debian-hosted mirrors; sources.list entries using `ftp://` now fail to update even before apt 2.9.11 removed the ftp method.
mechanism: Stretch release notes 5.1.2 "FTP access to Debian hosted mirrors will be removed" states verbatim: "Debian hosted mirrors will stop providing FTP access. If you have been using the ftp: protocol in your sources.list, please migrate to http:." This is the server-side retirement that, combined with the later client-side removal of the ftp method in apt 2.9.11, makes any `deb ftp://ftp.<country>.debian.org/debian ...` line unusable for building or installing packages on a modern Debian host.

actions.hint: Rewrite every `deb ftp://...` entry to `deb http://...` (or https:// for deb.debian.org). The stretch release notes give the canonical migration: `deb http://deb.debian.org/debian <suite> main` and `deb http://deb.debian.org/debian-security <suite>/updates main`.
If the sources.list is generated by an external tool you cannot edit, run a one-shot sed: `sed -i "s|^deb ftp://ftp\.\([^.]*\)\.debian\.org|deb http://deb.debian.org|" /etc/apt/sources.list`.

non_solutions: Installing apt-transport-ftp does not exist and the upstream mirror has stopped serving FTP anyway.

summary: Buster (10) is the first Debian release where /bin, /sbin, /lib are symlinks into /usr on fresh installs; legacy third-party software assuming these are separate directories can break on a fresh buster builder.
mechanism: Buster release notes 2.2.12 "Merged /usr on fresh installs" verbatim: "On fresh installs, the content of /bin, /sbin and /lib will be installed into their /usr counterpart by default. /bin, /sbin and /lib will be soft-links pointing at their directory counterpart under /usr/. When upgrading to buster, systems are left as they are, although the usrmerge package exists to do the conversion if desired. This change shouldn't impact normal users that only run packages provided by Debian, but it may be something that people that use or build third party software want to be aware of." Concretely: build scripts that copy/move files between /bin and /usr/bin (treating them as distinct filesystems), or that stat() the two paths to detect duplicates, see them as the same inode and misbehave.

actions.hint: For OLD projects that hard-fail on /bin==/usr/bin, run the build on a pre-buster (jessie/stretch) container where /bin, /sbin, /lib are real directories; or use an upgraded-not-fresh-installed buster (the upgrade preserves the legacy layout).
Patch the install/copy logic in the project Makefile/CMakeLists to tolerate symlinked /bin (e.g. cp -aT or use install(1)); never assume /bin and /usr/bin are on different filesystems.

non_solutions: Running the usrmerge conversion script does not help; it converts in the opposite direction (legacy to merged).

summary: Bookworm (12) makes merged-/usr MANDATORY: legacy-layout systems are auto-converted at dist-upgrade; dpkg --search on /usr/bin paths returns wrong answers, and third-party software assuming split layout must be fixed or removed before upgrade.
mechanism: Bookworm release notes 5.1.14 'A "merged-/usr" is now required': legacy directories /bin, /sbin, /lib, /lib64 are replaced with symlinks to /usr/bin, /usr/sbin, /usr/lib, /usr/lib64. Systems still on the legacy layout (e.g. an old host dist-upgraded in place from before buster) are converted when upgraded to bookworm. Known issues documented: (a) `dpkg --search /usr/bin/bash` does NOT identify the package while `dpkg --search /bin/bash` still works; (b) local software relying on /usr/bin/X and /bin/X being different files breaks; (c) WSL1 / overlayfs multilayer images cannot be safely converted and must be reinstalled or have each layer upgraded separately.

actions.hint: Fix `dpkg --search` calls in scripts/build pipelines to query the legacy path (/bin/bash, not /usr/bin/bash) — the symlink makes both resolve, but dpkg database uses the historical path.

For OLD third-party software that hard-requires /bin != /usr/bin, run the build on a non-merged-usr chroot (bullseye with the legacy layout) — but note bookworm itself no longer supports the legacy layout, so the host must be older.
For WSL1 / multilayer overlayfs images, replace the image from scratch or upgrade each layer independently rather than dist-upgrading; this avoids the unsafe conversion.

non_solutions: Trying to undo the merged-/usr symlinks after the upgrade is unsupported and breaks dpkg.
Editing C/C++ sources does not help; the failure is in the filesystem/packaging layer.

summary: Bookworm (12) split firmware packages out of `non-free` into a new `non-free-firmware` archive component; sources.list lines without it cause `E: Unable to locate package <firmware*>` and apt prints a NonFreeFirmware warning on every update.
mechanism: Bookworm release notes 2.2.8 / 5.1.1 document the split: firmware packages previously in non-free now live in non-free-firmware. apt update prints a warning suggesting to add the new component (APT::Get::Update::SourceListWarnings::NonFreeFirmware), and `apt install <firmware-package>` / `apt build-dep` for any source pulling firmware Build-Depends fails with `E: Unable to locate package firmware-...`. Trixie release notes 4.2.8 reaffirm: "If you have non-free firmware installed it is recommended to add non-free-firmware to your APT sources." apt 2.6.0 ("Suggest using non-free-firmware in update for Debian") is the first version to teach apt about the new component.
trigger_patterns: E: Unable to locate package firmware-
Packages in non-free have moved to the new non-free-firmware component
negative_patterns: E: Unable to locate package git

actions.hint: Add non-free-firmware to the components column of every Debian 12+ source entry. In one-line format: `deb http://deb.debian.org/debian bookworm main non-free-firmware`. In deb822: list it on the Components: line.

Silence the recurring NonFreeFirmware warning by creating /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/no-bookworm-firmware.conf with `APT::Get::Update::SourceListWarnings::NonFreeFirmware "false";` (only if you genuinely do not need firmware).
Pin the build to Debian bullseye (no firmware split) while the build-config is updated.

non_solutions: Re-adding non-free does not bring back the firmware packages; they live in non-free-firmware now.

summary: Skip-upgrading directly from buster (10) to bookworm (12) fails during libc6 setup with `libcrypt.so.1: cannot open shared object file`; only single-step upgrades (bullseye to bookworm) are supported.
mechanism: Bookworm release notes 5.1.15 "Unsupported upgrades from buster fail on libcrypt1" verbatim: "Debian officially supports upgrades only from one stable release to the next, e.g. from bullseye to bookworm. Upgrades from buster to bookworm are not supported, and will fail due to Bug #993755 with the following error: `Setting up libc6:amd64 (2.36-9) ... /usr/bin/perl: error while loading shared libraries: libcrypt.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory / dpkg: error processing package libc6:amd64 (--configure): installed libc6:amd64 package post-installation script subprocess returned error exit status 127`." Once libc6 fails to configure, no further apt operation succeeds and the build environment is wedged.
trigger_patterns: /usr/bin/perl: error while loading shared libraries: libcrypt.so.1: cannot open shared object file
libcrypt.so.1: cannot open shared object file
installed libc6:amd64 package post-installation script subprocess returned error exit status 127
negative_patterns: E: Could not perform immediate configuration

actions.hint: Recover by manually installing the new libcrypt1 first: `cd $(mktemp -d) && apt download libcrypt1 && dpkg-deb -x libcrypt1_*.deb . && cp -ra lib/* /lib/` — exactly as documented in the release notes — then re-run apt-get -f install and continue the upgrade.
Provision a clean bullseye -> bookworm path (single-step) instead of jumping buster -> bookworm; this is the only officially supported upgrade.

non_solutions: Reinstalling libc6 by hand with dpkg -i makes it worse; the perl runtime cannot start because libcrypt is missing.

summary: During the trixie upgrade dpkg prints `dpkg: warning: unable to delete old directory '/lib/firmware/<x>': Directory not empty` for many packages because of the usrmerge finalization; the warnings can be safely ignored but pollute logs.
mechanism: Trixie release notes 5.1.24 "dpkg: warning: unable to delete old directory: ..." verbatim: "During the upgrade, dpkg will print warnings like the following, for various packages. This is due to the finalization of the usrmerge project, and the warnings can be safely ignored." Example: `Unpacking firmware-misc-nonfree (...) over (...) ... dpkg: warning: unable to delete old directory '/lib/firmware/wfx': Directory not empty / dpkg: warning: unable to delete old directory '/lib/firmware/ueagle-atm': Directory not empty`. Although benign, naive CI that treats any dpkg warning as fatal will fail the build unnecessarily.
trigger_patterns: dpkg: warning: unable to delete old directory '/lib/firmware/
dpkg: warning: unable to delete old directory

actions.hint: If your CI scraper treats dpkg warnings as fatal, filter the benign `unable to delete old directory ... Directory not empty` lines from the upgrade log (e.g. apt-get dist-upgrade 2>&1 | grep -v 'unable to delete old directory'). Per the release notes the warnings need no remediation.
Post-upgrade, run `dpkg --configure -a && apt-get -f install` to confirm there are no real errors; the warnings themselves do not indicate a broken state.

non_solutions: Manually rm -rf the firmware directories is wrong — they are real package content; dpkg will recreate them.
Forcing --force-remove-reinstreq does not apply here.

summary: Trixie explicitly does not support skip-upgrades; the usrmerge finalization requires the system to be at bookworm first, so bullseye to trixie jumps fail.
mechanism: Trixie release notes 5.1.25 "Skip-upgrades are not supported" verbatim: "As with any other Debian release, upgrades must be performed from the previous release. Also all point release updates should be installed. ... Skipping releases when upgrading is explicitly not supported. For trixie, the finalization of the usrmerge project requires the upgrade to bookworm be completed before starting the trixie upgrade." Trying to jump bullseye -> trixie (or older -> trixie) leads to broken dpkg state, unpack errors and an unbootable build container.
trigger_patterns: Skipping releases when upgrading is explicitly not supported
requires the upgrade to bookworm be completed before starting the trixie upgrade
negative_patterns: E: Could not perform immediate configuration
libcrypt.so.1: cannot open shared object file

actions.hint: Provision the build host through the supported path: bullseye -> bookworm -> trixie (full-upgrade each step, all point releases applied).
If you must reuse an old image, snapshot it after the bookworm full-upgrade completes, then run the trixie upgrade; never combine them in one apt invocation.

non_solutions: Manually installing the usrmerge package on bullseye does not make the skip-upgrade supported; dpkg will still fail.

summary: Starting in trixie, the .gpg keyring paths referenced by Signed-By are backwards-compat symlinks to the canonical .pgp paths; the symlinks will eventually disappear, breaking sources that hard-code .gpg.
mechanism: Trixie release notes 4.3.1 / 4.3.2 / 4.7 document repeatedly: "Starting in trixie the .gpg keyring pathnames are now backwards compatibility symlinks to the new .pgp canonical pathnames, which will eventually get removed." Section 4.7 (Cleanup after the upgrade) recommends: "Switch your APT sources to use the canonical Debian archive keyring pathnames in Signed-By, by replacing the .gpg extension to .pgp, as the backwards compatible .gpg symlinks will eventually disappear." An OLD project setup script that hard-codes `Signed-By: /usr/share/keyrings/debian-archive-keyring.gpg` will keep working today but will silently break once the symlink is removed.

actions.hint: In every deb822 .sources file (and every signed-by= on one-line entries), replace the trailing .gpg with .pgp for canonical Debian archive keyrings, e.g. `Signed-By: /usr/share/keyrings/debian-archive-keyring.pgp`. Then verify with apt update.
Run `apt modernize-sources` (apt >= 2.9.26) once; it rewrites paths to the canonical form.

non_solutions: Re-creating the .gpg file from the .pgp keeps things working today but re-introduces the deprecated suffix that apt will refuse later.

summary: Packages put on hold (via dpkg --set-selections or aptitude) abort the dist-upgrade with "package that is essential for the upgrade is on hold, the upgrade will fail" until all holds are removed.
mechanism: Jessie release notes 4.2.3 ("It is desirable to remove any holds before upgrading. If any package that is essential for the upgrade is on hold, the upgrade will fail.") and the corresponding 4.2.3 sections in stretch/buster/bullseye/bookworm document this rule. Old build hosts that locally recompiled a package and held it (or where a third-party repo held back a package) cannot pass the dist-upgrade step that builds need to provision. apt-get and aptitude use different hold stores (apt-get uses dpkg --get-selections, aptitude uses its own ~ahold), so holds can hide from one tool while still blocking the other.
trigger_patterns: package that is essential for the upgrade is on hold
The following packages have been kept back
negative_patterns: E: Could not perform immediate configuration

actions.hint: List and remove all holds before the upgrade: `apt-mark showhold | xargs -r apt-mark unhold` (modern apt). For dpkg-level holds: `dpkg --get-selections | grep hold$` then `echo <pkg> install | dpkg --set-selections`. For aptitude holds: `aptitude search "~ahold"` then `aptitude unhold <pkg>`.
If a hold is intentional (e.g. locally rebuilt gcc), snapshot the system, perform the upgrade without the hold, then re-apply the hold afterwards.

non_solutions: Forcing `apt-get -f install` does not clear holds; the hold flag is independent of the dependency state.
Switching to aptitude does not bypass the rule; aptitude has its own hold concept and the upgrade still aborts.

summary: A Conflicts/Pre-Depends loop among essential packages aborts apt-get dist-upgrade asking the user to pass `-o APT::Force-LoopBreak=1`; without it the upgrade cannot proceed.
mechanism: Wheezy release notes 4.5.4 "Conflicts or Pre-Depends loops" (and similar sections in later releases) document verbatim: "Sometimes it's necessary to enable the APT::Force-LoopBreak option in APT to be able to temporarily remove an essential package due to a Conflicts/Pre-Depends loop. apt-get will alert you of this and abort the upgrade. You can work around this by specifying the option -o APT::Force-LoopBreak=1 on the apt-get command line." This happens most often when an OLD third-party apt repo forces an essential package version into the resolver; the build cannot proceed to compile anything until the loop is broken.
trigger_patterns: essential package due to a Conflicts

actions.hint: Re-run the failing command with -o APT::Force-LoopBreak=1, exactly as the release notes recommend: `apt-get -o APT::Force-LoopBreak=1 dist-upgrade`. This lets apt temporarily remove an essential package to break the loop.
If the loop is caused by a third-party source, remove or downgrade that source from sources.list.d before retrying the upgrade.
For fully broken states the release notes give the recovery sequence: `dpkg --remove <pkg>`, then `apt-get -f install`, then `dpkg --configure --pending`, then `dpkg --install /path/to/<pkg>.deb`.

non_solutions: Switching to aptitude does not bypass an essential-package loop; both solvers honor the same Conflicts/Pre-Depends constraint.

summary: Mixing unofficial backports into sources.list causes `trying to overwrite '/usr/...' which is also in package <other>` during dist-upgrade, blocking the build-dependency install.
mechanism: Wheezy release notes 4.5.5 "File conflicts" (and analogous sections in later releases) document verbatim: "File conflicts should not occur if you upgrade from a \"pure\" squeeze system, but can occur if you have unofficial backports installed. A file conflict will result in an error like: `Unpacking <package-foo> (from <package-foo-file>) ... dpkg: error processing <package-foo-file> (--unpack): trying to overwrite \'<path>\" which is also in package <package-bar>`." OLD build hosts that pulled a third-party -dev backport (typical for C/C++ library workarounds) hit this when a newer Debian version owns the same file. The build-dependency step (`apt build-dep`) fails before any compilation starts.
trigger_patterns: dpkg-deb: error: paste subprocess was killed

actions.hint: Instruct dpkg to accept the overwrite for the offending package: `apt-get -o Dpkg::Options::="--force-overwrite" install <pkgs>` (or dist-upgrade).
Remove the unofficial backport lines from /etc/apt/sources.list.d first, then `apt-get update && apt-get -f install` to let Debian own package versions take precedence.
If the conflict is between two Debian-provided packages and you really need the third-party one, `dpkg --force-overwrite -i /var/cache/apt/archives/<pkg>.deb` forces the local install.

non_solutions: Re-running apt-get update alone does not resolve the conflict; dpkg has already refused the unpack.

summary: Each Debian release removes obsolete packages and replaces some with dummies; reinstalling them on a newer release fails with `E: Unable to locate package <X>` and the dummy packages themselves become redundant.
mechanism: The "Obsolete packages" sections of every Debian release (etch 4.10 / lenny 4.10 / squeeze 4.9 / wheezy 4.8 / jessie 4.10 / stretch 4.8 / buster 4.8 / bullseye 4.8 / bookworm 4.8) document a curated list of packages that no longer exist in the new archive or exist only as transitional dummies. Concrete C/C++-relevant removals across releases: python2.5, python3.2, ruby1.8/1.9.1, mysql-5.1, postgresql-8.4/9.1, sun-java6, mplayer, openoffice.org, squid, portmap, gdm, the historic Xorg drivers. Reinstalling any of these (`apt install python2.5`, `apt build-dep -y mysql-5.1`) on a newer Debian release returns `E: Unable to locate package ...`, blocking the build-dependency provisioning of an OLD project.
negative_patterns: E: Could not perform immediate configuration

actions.hint: Map the missing package to its documented successor (release notes per release): python2.5 -> python2.7, python3.2 -> python3.4, ruby1.8/1.9.1 -> ruby2.1, mysql-5.1 -> mysql-5.5, postgresql-8.4 -> postgresql-9.1, sun-java6 -> openjdk-7, portmap -> rpcbind, mplayer -> mplayer2/mpv, openoffice.org -> libreoffice, squid -> squid3. Update the project build-dependencies accordingly.

For genuinely dead -dev packages, provision them from archive.debian.org: enable `deb http://archive.debian.org/debian <old-codename> main` and pin with /etc/apt/preferences.d (Pin: release o=Debian,a=<old-codename>; Pin-Priority: 100).
For "dummy" packages (empty transitional wrappers), the release notes document they can be safely removed after the upgrade (`apt purge $(deborphan --guess-dummy)` or `aptitude purge ~gbummy`).

non_solutions: Re-adding the suite name to sources.list does not resurrect packages physically removed from the archive.
Editing the project C/C++ source does not help; the failure is at the build-dependency install step.

summary: apt 2.7+ honors Phased-Update-Percentage, so a randomly-chosen fraction of hosts do not get a package update on `apt upgrade`; build environments can be silently stuck on an older -dev version.
mechanism: apt 2.1.16 added "Add support for Phased-Update-Percentage, previously used only by ..." and 2.7.11 ("Show a separate list of upgrades deferred due to phasing") made the behaviour visible. By default apt on Debian/Ubuntu randomly defers phased updates per machine (seeded by machine-id) — this means `apt upgrade` may report packages as "kept back" / "deferred due to phasing" with no actual dependency conflict. For reproducible builds and CI this is a major foot-gun: an OLD project that builds fine on developer machine A may fail on CI machine B simply because machine B received a newer -dev.
negative_patterns: E: Could not perform immediate configuration

actions.hint: Force all phased updates to install on a build host: `apt-get -o APT::Get::Always-Include-Phased-Updates=true update && apt-get upgrade`, or set APT::Get::Always-Include-Phased-Updates "true"; permanently in /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/. This makes machine-specific phasing a no-op.
For CI reproducibility, pin the exact package version you want with /etc/apt/preferences.d (Pin-Priority) instead of relying on whatever apt upgrade picks.

non_solutions: Re-running apt update alone does not change the phasing decision; the seed is the machine-id.

summary: Autoconf 2.70+ AC_CHECK_HEADER only does compilation test, may miss headers with unmet dependencies
mechanism: AC_CHECK_HEADER and AC_CHECK_HEADERS now only perform a compilation test (no longer a preprocess-then-compile double test). Headers that exist but cannot be compiled (due to missing prerequisite headers or packages) will now silently report 'no' instead of the previous 'present but cannot be compiled' warning. This can cause HAVE_xxx_H to not be defined, leading to compilation failures in the project's own code.

actions.hint: Add proper prerequisite headers to the AC_CHECK_HEADERS fourth argument (includes parameter). For example: AC_CHECK_HEADERS([net/if.h], [], [], [#include <sys/socket.h>])

summary: Autoconf 2.70+ AC_OPENMP errors out if files named 'mp' or 'penmp' exist in the directory
mechanism: Autoconf 2.70 will now issue an error if AC_OPENMP is used in a configure script that is in the same directory as a file named 'mp' or 'penmp'. Configure scripts using AC_OPENMP will also error out upon encountering files with these names in their working directory.

actions.hint: Rename or move files named 'mp' or 'penmp' at the top level of the source tree into a subdirectory.

summary: Autoconf 2.70+ reduces AC_REQUIRE dependencies, exposing latent macro ordering bugs
mechanism: Many macros no longer AC_REQUIRE as many other macros as they used to. This exposes latent bugs in configure.ac where macros that set result variables are not explicitly invoked, or where AC_REQUIRE-using macros are placed inside shell control-flow constructs (if/case) outside of AC_DEFUN. The fix is to use AS_IF/AS_CASE instead of shell if/case, and to explicitly invoke all required prerequisite macros.
trigger_patterns: AC_REQUIRE should not be used outside of

actions.hint: Replace shell if/case constructs wrapping autoconf macros with AS_IF/AS_CASE in configure.ac. Explicitly invoke all prerequisite macros (e.g., AC_PROG_CC) before macros that depend on their results.

summary: Setting CC to a C++ compiler (e.g., CC=g++) is no longer supported in autoconf 2.70+, causing configure tests to produce incorrect results.
mechanism: Autoconf 2.70 explicitly documents that setting CC to a C++ compiler is unsupported. Configure tests that probe C-specific behavior (like implicit function declarations, sizeof checks, or header availability) will produce wrong results when CC is a C++ compiler because C++ has different semantics. This was never guaranteed to work but was tolerated in older versions. Projects that set CC=g++ or CC=c++ in their build scripts will get incorrect configure results leading to compile failures.
trigger_patterns: configure: error: C compiler cannot create executables

actions.hint: Do not set CC to a C++ compiler. Use CXX for C++ compilation and CC for C compilation separately.
Use older autoconf < 2.70 where this was silently tolerated

non_solutions: Adding AC_PROG_CXX does not help if the project sets CC=g++ explicitly

summary: Autoconf 2.70+ configure tests fail when CC includes -Werror or CFLAGS contains -Werror
mechanism: Running configure tests with warnings promoted to errors is explicitly not supported in autoconf 2.70+. Setting CC='gcc -Werror' or adding -Werror to CFLAGS early in configure will cause subsequent AC_CHECK_FUNC and similar tests to fail because the generated test code triggers compiler warnings (e.g., implicit function declarations). This was always fragile but is more likely to fail with newer autoconf and newer compilers.

actions.hint: Remove -Werror from CFLAGS/CC in configure.ac. Instead, use a dedicated WARN_CFLAGS variable set via AC_SUBST that is only applied to the project's own code in Makefile.am, not during configure tests.
Remove -Werror from CFLAGS when running configure: CFLAGS without -Werror

summary: Autoconf 2.70+ is stricter about macro argument quotation, causing shell syntax errors in generated configure
mechanism: Many macros have become pickier about argument quotation in autoconf 2.70. If configure.ac has improperly quoted macro arguments, the generated configure script may contain shell syntax errors or exhibit seemingly impossible misbehavior (e.g. entire blocks not getting executed). autoupdate cannot correct quotation errors.
trigger_patterns: syntax error: unexpected end of file

actions.hint: Fix macro argument quotation in configure.ac. Ensure all macro arguments are properly quoted with square brackets per M4 quotation rules. For example, change AC_INIT(mypackage, 1.0) to AC_INIT([mypackage], [1.0]).
As a temporary workaround, regenerate configure using an older autoconf version by setting AUTOCONF=autoconf-2.69 before running autoreconf.

summary: Autoconf 2.70+ requires config.sub and config.guess for more macros, causing autoreconf failures
mechanism: More macros now use config.sub and config.guess internally in autoconf 2.70. Old projects that did not previously need these auxiliary scripts may now fail during autoreconf because the scripts cannot be found. autoreconf will issue an error if any auxiliary scripts are needed but cannot be found.

actions.hint: Run autoreconf with --install flag to automatically add config.sub, config.guess, and install-sh to the source tree: autoreconf --install --force

summary: AC_PROG_CC no longer checks __STDC__ or variable length arrays (VLAs), which may break configure scripts that relied on these checks being performed by AC_PROG_CC.
mechanism: Projects whose configure.ac relied on AC_PROG_CC setting variables or defines related to __STDC__ compliance or VLA support will no longer get those results. Code that conditionally used VLAs based on AC_PROG_CC's detection will need to explicitly call AC_C_VARARRAYS instead.
trigger_patterns: error:.*(forbids variable length array|variable-sized object|variable length array)

actions.hint: Add AC_C_VARARRAYS to configure.ac if VLA detection is needed, and stop relying on AC_PROG_CC to define __STDC__.
Use autoconf < 2.72.90 (Debian stable ships 2.71/2.72).

non_solutions: Defining __STDC__ manually (compiler-defined macro)

summary: AC_PROG_CC now prefers C23 if available, breaking old code that uses K&R function definitions, implicit int, or identifiers that became keywords (bool, true, false, alignas, etc.).
mechanism: Autoconf 2.72.90 changed AC_PROG_CC to select C23 mode by default when the compiler supports it. C23 removes K&R function definitions, implicit function declarations, and introduces new keywords (bool, true, false, alignas, alignof, constexpr, nullptr, static_assert, thread_local, typeof). Old C code using these as variable/function names or relying on removed syntax will fail to compile.

actions.hint: Use autoconf < 2.72.90 or pass CC='gcc -std=gnu11' to configure to override the C23 default

non_solutions: Upgrading the compiler (the issue is the C standard mode, not compiler version)
Adding -std=c23 flags (this makes the problem worse for old code)

summary: AC_PROG_CXX no longer attempts to switch to C++98 or C++11, using the compiler's default instead, which may break projects requiring older C++ standards.
mechanism: Previously AC_PROG_CXX would attempt to force C++98 or C++11 mode. Now it uses the compiler's default (typically C++17 or C++20 in modern compilers). Projects relying on C++98/C++11 specific behavior or using features removed in later standards (auto_ptr, register keyword, throw() exception specifications) will fail to compile.

actions.hint: Use autoconf < 2.72.90 or pass CXX='g++ -std=gnu++11' to configure to force older C++ standard

non_solutions: Upgrading the C++ compiler (the issue is the default standard mode, not compiler version)

summary: Autoconf 2.72 removed all internal uses of AC_EGREP_CPP/AC_EGREP_HEADER, breaking configure scripts that relied on grep/preprocessor probes happening as side effects of unrelated macros.
mechanism: Macros like AC_C_STRINGIZE, AC_C_VARARRAYS, AC_FUNC_GETGROUPS, AC_FUNC_GETLOADAVG, AC_HEADER_TIOCGWINSZ, AC_PROG_GCC_TRADITIONAL, AC_TYPE_GETGROUPS, AC_TYPE_UID_T, and AC_XENIX_DIR no longer internally invoke AC_EGREP_CPP. Configure scripts that depended on AC_PROG_EGREP or AC_PROG_CPP being set as a side effect of these macros will fail with 'EGREP: command not found' or similar.

actions.hint: Add explicit AC_PROG_EGREP and/or AC_PROG_CPP calls in configure.ac before macros that previously relied on them as a side effect (AC_C_STRINGIZE, AC_C_VARARRAYS, AC_FUNC_GETLOADAVG, etc.).
Use autoconf < 2.72.

non_solutions: Installing grep (it is already installed; the issue is the configure variable not being set)

summary: Automake 1.11 added a configure-time sanity check that fails if the absolute source directory path contains unsafe characters (spaces, special characters).
mechanism: The AM_SANITY_CHECK macro now validates the source directory path at configure time. If the absolute path contains spaces or other unsafe characters, configure will fail immediately with a diagnostic message, even though the project itself is valid.

actions.hint: Move the source tree to a path without spaces or special characters, or use automake < 1.11

non_solutions: Quoting the path in the build command (the check is inside configure itself)

summary: The 'cygnus' option for Cygnus-style trees is deprecated in 1.12.1 and removed in 1.13, causing autoreconf failure for projects using it.
mechanism: Projects with AM_INIT_AUTOMAKE([cygnus]) or the cygnus option in Makefile.am trigger an obsolete warning (error with -Werror) in 1.12.1 and a hard failure in 1.13+ because the option is no longer recognized.

actions.hint: Remove 'cygnus' from AM_INIT_AUTOMAKE / AUTOMAKE_OPTIONS and restructure the Cygnus-style tree layout to the standard GNU layout.
Use older Debian with automake <= 1.12 (e.g. wheezy) to retain cygnus support.

non_solutions: Simply removing the cygnus option may require restructuring the entire build tree layout

summary: The $(mkdir_p) variable, @mkdir_p@ substitution, and AM_PROG_MKDIR macro are deprecated with warnings that become errors under -Werror.
mechanism: Projects using $(mkdir_p) in Makefile.am or AM_PROG_MKDIR in configure.ac trigger obsolete-category warnings in automake >= 1.12.1. With -Werror or obsolete warnings promoted to errors, autoreconf fails.
trigger_patterns: automake: error: '$(mkdir_p)' is no longer supported
automake: error: 'AM_PROG_MKDIR' is no longer supported

actions.hint: Replace $(mkdir_p) with $(MKDIR_P) in Makefile.am and remove AM_PROG_MKDIR from configure.ac.
Use older Debian with automake <= 1.11 where $(mkdir_p) and AM_PROG_MKDIR are still supported without warnings.

non_solutions: Suppressing warnings with -Wno-obsolete only delays the issue as these are removed in later versions

summary: Obsolete-category warnings are now enabled by default in automake and aclocal, causing autoreconf failure for projects using -Werror.
mechanism: Projects that use deprecated constructs (e.g., AM_PROG_MKDIR, $(mkdir_p), cygnus option) and have -Werror in AUTOMAKE_OPTIONS or AM_INIT_AUTOMAKE will now fail during autoreconf because obsolete warnings are emitted by default and promoted to errors.
trigger_patterns: automake: warnings are treated as errors

actions.hint: Add -Wno-obsolete to AUTOMAKE_OPTIONS, or fix the obsolete construct the warning points at.
Use older Debian with automake <= 1.12.3 where obsolete warnings are not enabled by default.

non_solutions: Adding -Wno-obsolete may mask real issues that cause failures in later automake versions

summary: Yacc/Lex derived files from non-distributed sources are now removed by 'make clean' instead of only 'make maintainer-clean', breaking incremental build workflows.
mechanism: Projects that rely on generated Yacc/Lex C files persisting across 'make clean' cycles (e.g., for bootstrapping without yacc/lex installed) will find those files deleted, causing subsequent builds to fail if yacc/lex is unavailable.

actions.hint: List the generated Yacc/Lex .c/.h outputs in EXTRA_DIST, or ensure yacc/lex (bison/flex) are installed so 'make clean' no longer strands the build.
Use older Debian with automake <= 1.11 where Yacc/Lex derived files survive make clean.

non_solutions: Adding generated files to EXTRA_DIST changes distribution semantics

summary: Automake 1.12 removed support for automatic de-ANSI-fication (ansi2knr), causing errors for projects using AM_C_PROTOTYPES or AUTOMAKE_OPTIONS = ansi2knr.
mechanism: Automake 1.12 removed the de-ANSI-fication feature that allowed K&R C compilers to build ANSI C code via the ansi2knr program. Projects that have AM_C_PROTOTYPES in configure.ac or 'ansi2knr' in AUTOMAKE_OPTIONS will fail when running automake 1.12+. The AM_C_PROTOTYPES macro is no longer defined, and the ansi2knr option is no longer recognized.

actions.hint: Remove AM_C_PROTOTYPES from configure.ac and remove 'ansi2knr' from AUTOMAKE_OPTIONS in Makefile.am. Modern compilers all support ANSI C.
Use older Debian with automake < 1.12

non_solutions: Providing a custom ansi2knr script will not help since automake no longer generates the rules to invoke it

summary: Automake 1.12 removed the deprecated 'lzma' distribution format; projects using dist-lzma in AUTOMAKE_OPTIONS will fail.
mechanism: Automake 1.12 removed the 'lzma' compression format for distribution archives (deprecated in favor of 'xz' and 'lzip'). Projects with 'dist-lzma' in their Makefile.am AUTOMAKE_OPTIONS or configure.ac AM_INIT_AUTOMAKE options will get an unrecognized option error from automake.

actions.hint: Replace 'dist-lzma' with 'dist-xz' in AUTOMAKE_OPTIONS or AM_INIT_AUTOMAKE arguments
Use older Debian with automake < 1.12

summary: Yacc C++ header file extensions changed to match source extensions, breaking builds that expect the old .h naming.
mechanism: In automake >= 1.12, a Yacc source named foo.y++ produces foo.h++ instead of foo.h, and bar.yy produces bar.hh instead of bar.h. Projects with #include directives referencing the old header names fail to compile.

actions.hint: Rename the Yacc C++ source to a plain .y extension, or update #include / Makefile references from the old .h to the new modelled extension (.h++/.hh).
Use older Debian with automake <= 1.11 where Yacc C++ headers always use the .h extension.

non_solutions: Renaming only the Yacc source without updating all #include references

summary: AM_CONFIG_HEADER and AM_PROG_CC_STDC macros were removed in automake 1.13, causing fatal errors during autoreconf.
mechanism: Automake 1.13 removed the obsolete macros AM_CONFIG_HEADER and AM_PROG_CC_STDC, causing configure.ac files that use them to fail with fatal warnings. Fixed in 1.13.2 which restored them as deprecated warnings.

actions.hint: Replace AM_CONFIG_HEADER with AC_CONFIG_HEADERS and AM_PROG_CC_STDC with AC_PROG_CC in configure.ac.
Use automake >= 1.13.2 where these macros are restored as deprecated, or stay on automake 1.12.x.

summary: The shar and tarZ distribution formats (dist-shar, dist-tarZ options) are obsolescent and deprecated in the documentation as of automake 1.13.2; automake 1.14+ additionally emits obsolete-category warnings at automake runtime, with full removal scheduled for Automake 2.0.
mechanism: In automake 1.13.2, dist-shar and dist-tarZ in Makefile.am are merely deprecated in the documentation (no runtime warning yet). Starting with automake 1.14, their use triggers obsolete-category warnings at automake runtime and non-fatal warnings at make runtime; the formats are scheduled for removal in Automake 2.0, not in any 1.x release.

actions.hint: Replace dist-shar/dist-tarZ with dist-xz or dist-bzip2 in Makefile.am AUTOMAKE_OPTIONS.
Use automake < 1.13.2.

summary: Automake 1.13 removed all old alias macros from m4/obsolete.m4, causing undefined macro errors for projects using legacy macro names.
mechanism: Automake 1.13 removed all macros from m4/obsolete.m4 including fp_PROG_CC_STDC, fp_WITH_DMALLOC, ud_PATH_LISPDIR, jm_MAINTAINER_MODE, ud_GNU_GETTEXT, gm_PROG_LIBTOOL, fp_C_PROTOTYPES, and others. Projects using any of these ancient macro aliases in configure.ac will get 'possibly undefined macro' errors during autoreconf.

actions.hint: Replace legacy macro aliases with their modern equivalents: fp_PROG_CC_STDC→AC_PROG_CC, fp_WITH_DMALLOC→AM_WITH_DMALLOC, ud_PATH_LISPDIR→AM_PATH_LISPDIR, jm_MAINTAINER_MODE→AM_MAINTAINER_MODE, ud_GNU_GETTEXT→AM_GNU_GETTEXT, gm_PROG_LIBTOOL→AC_PROG_LIBTOOL, fp_C_PROTOTYPES→(remove, no longer needed)
Use older Debian with automake < 1.13

summary: The 'compile' script is now unconditionally required for all packages that perform C compilation in automake 1.14+, causing errors if the script is missing and --add-missing is not used.
mechanism: Previously, the 'compile' script was only needed when AM_PROG_CC_C_O detected a compiler that didn't support combined -c -o options. Starting with automake 1.14, it is unconditionally required for any package performing C compilation. Projects that run automake without --add-missing (or autoreconf without --install) and lack the compile script will get a hard error.

actions.hint: Run 'autoreconf --install --force' or 'automake --add-missing' to have automake fetch the compile script automatically
Use older Debian with automake < 1.14 where compile script is only conditionally required

non_solutions: Manually creating a dummy compile script

summary: AM_INIT_AUTOMAKE now aborts configure if 'rm -f' (without file arguments) returns an error, which fails on some non-standard systems.
mechanism: The shell code expanded by AM_INIT_AUTOMAKE checks at configure runtime that 'rm -f' with no file argument acts as a no-op. If the system rm does not support this, configure aborts with an error about a broken rm program.
negative_patterns: rm: No such file or directory

actions.hint: set ACCEPT_INFERIOR_RM_PROGRAM=yes or use a system where rm -f without args is a no-op

non_solutions: ignoring the error

summary: make distcheck now uses a deeper build subdirectory, changing $(srcdir) from '..' to '../..', breaking Makefiles that hardcode distcheck path assumptions.
mechanism: distcheck uses '$(distdir)/_build/sub' instead of '$(distdir)/_build' as build directory, so $(srcdir) becomes '../..' instead of '..'. Makefiles with hardcoded relative paths to source files during distcheck will fail.
trigger_patterns: (No such file or directory|No rule to make target).*\.\./\.\.

actions.hint: Fix Makefile.am to not hardcode relative $(srcdir) paths for distcheck (it now runs from _build/sub, so srcdir is ../..).
Use automake < 1.15.

non_solutions: setting srcdir manually

summary: Automake 1.6 requires Autoconf 2.52+, removes several AM_ macros (AM_FUNC_ERROR_AT_LINE, AM_FUNC_STRTOD, AM_FUNC_OBSTACK, AM_PTRDIFF_T), and changes the assembler variable from AS to CCAS.
mechanism: Automake 1.6 requires Autoconf 2.52+. The AM_FUNC_ERROR_AT_LINE, AM_FUNC_STRTOD, AM_FUNC_OBSTACK and AM_PTRDIFF_T macros are no longer shipped by Automake (Autoconf 2.52 provides them both as AM_ and AC_ forms), so errors only arise when an older Autoconf (< 2.52) is used. The compiler-based assembler variable was renamed from AS to CCAS, and the old two-argument 'AC_INIT AM_INIT_AUTOMAKE(tarname,version)' form is obsolete.

actions.hint: Replace AM_FUNC_ERROR_AT_LINE with AC_FUNC_ERROR_AT_LINE, AM_FUNC_STRTOD with AC_FUNC_STRTOD, AM_FUNC_OBSTACK with AC_FUNC_OBSTACK, AM_PTRDIFF_T with AC_TYPE_PTRDIFF_T in configure.ac
Use older Debian with automake < 1.6

non_solutions: Ignoring the undefined macro warnings

summary: Automake 1.7 moves info files to build directory and enforces DESTDIR support in distcheck, breaking projects that assume info in srcdir or lack DESTDIR support.
mechanism: Info files created in build directory instead of source directory breaks projects expecting them in srcdir; distcheck now enforces DESTDIR install which fails if install targets use absolute paths without DESTDIR prefix.

actions.hint: Make uninstall rules DESTDIR-clean (so distcheck's distuninstallcheck passes) and stop assuming .info files live in srcdir.
Use older Debian with automake < 1.7.

non_solutions: ignoring distcheck failures

summary: AM_PROG_CC_STDC macro is now empty; configure.ac scripts referencing $am_cv_prog_cc_stdc will get an empty value.
mechanism: AM_PROG_CC_STDC no longer sets $am_cv_prog_cc_stdc; configure scripts or Makefile.am that test this variable will get empty/undefined results, potentially causing configure logic failures.

actions.hint: Update configure.ac / Makefile.am to use $ac_cv_prog_cc_stdc instead of the now-empty $am_cv_prog_cc_stdc.
Use automake < 1.8.

non_solutions: simply removing AM_PROG_CC_STDC call without updating variable references

summary: Bundled config.guess/config.sub exists but is too old to recognize the current build/host system.
mechanism: Old source releases often vendor config.guess and config.sub. On newer architectures or OS triples these scripts can fail even though the files exist, causing configure to abort before compilation.

actions.hint: Replace every bundled config.guess and config.sub with current GNU config versions before running configure.
Temporary workaround: pass an explicit canonical --build/--host triplet such as $(gcc -dumpmachine) when appropriate.

summary: Automake parallel-tests requires test-driver; old projects fail when automake is rerun without installing auxiliary scripts.
mechanism: Automake 1.12 switched the parallel test harness to an external test-driver script. Rebootstrap workflows that do not use --add-missing can fail with a required-file diagnostic.

actions.hint: Run autoreconf -fi or automake --add-missing --copy so test-driver is installed.

summary: Automake warns about sources in subdirectories without subdir-objects; -Werror turns this into a bootstrap failure.
mechanism: Automake 1.14 emits unsupported-category warnings when source files live in subdirectories but subdir-objects is disabled. Many projects run automake with -Werror during autoreconf.

actions.hint: Add subdir-objects to AUTOMAKE_OPTIONS or adjust Makefile.am source layout.

summary: Automake parallel-tests rejects invalid TEST_EXTENSIONS definitions that older projects could get away with.
mechanism: Automake 1.11.2 tightened diagnostics around TEST_EXTENSIONS; invalid or conditional definitions now fail with variable-name/redefinition diagnostics during automake.

actions.hint: Make TEST_EXTENSIONS a static valid extension list and move conditional logic into TESTS or driver scripts.

summary: aclocal --install can replace local m4 macros by higher-serial system copies, changing bootstrap behavior.
mechanism: aclocal --install copies third-party .m4 files into the local macro directory and may update them based on #serial. That can expose new macro semantics, undefined macro failures, or macro redefinition errors.

actions.hint: Pin and review local m4/*.m4 files; use aclocal --diff before installing newer system macros.

summary: Automake/aclocal switched local macro handling to m4_include, exposing missing or undistributed m4 files.
mechanism: Projects that relied on old aclocal behavior copying macro contents can fail after aclocal.m4 starts including local macro files by path.

actions.hint: Run aclocal -I m4 or autoreconf -fi, and ensure included m4/*.m4 files exist and are distributed.

summary: Standalone find_library() function was removed and is now a hard error in meson >= 0.45.0.
mechanism: Old meson.build files using the standalone find_library() call (not via compiler object) will fail with a hard error during meson setup because the function was removed.

actions.hint: Use a Debian release with meson < 0.45.0 (e.g., Debian stretch has meson 0.37)

non_solutions: Modifying the project meson.build to use compiler.find_library() is source modification and not allowed

summary: Keywordless run_target() syntax was removed and is now a hard error in meson >= 0.45.0.
mechanism: Old meson.build files using run_target('name', 'command', 'arg1') without the command: keyword will fail during meson setup because the positional argument form was removed.

actions.hint: Use a Debian release with meson < 0.45.0 (e.g., Debian stretch has meson 0.37)

non_solutions: Modifying run_target() calls to use keyword syntax is source modification and not allowed

summary: Meson 0.48.0 added a native: keyword to add_global_arguments/add_global_link_arguments/add_project_arguments/add_project_link_arguments so args can be scoped to native vs cross targets. Default (no native:) still applies to BOTH native and cross; breakage is rare and only affects projects that relied on the old undifferentiated behavior.
mechanism: Meson 0.48.0 introduced the native: keyword on the add_*_arguments functions to let project args be set separately for cross and native builds. Without native: the flags are still passed to both native and cross compilations, so widespread breakage is uncommon; only projects with unusual reliance on the old behavior are affected.

actions.hint: Use a Debian release with meson < 0.48.0 (e.g., Debian stretch/buster with older meson)

non_solutions: Adding native: keyword to add_project_arguments calls is source modification and not allowed

summary: Meson 0.52.0 simplified the native flag on add_global_arguments/add_global_link_arguments/add_project_arguments/add_project_link_arguments so that omitting native: now equals native:false (host machine only), matching the c_args vs build_c_args build/host model. Native builds that relied on add_project_arguments applying by default lose those flags.
mechanism: Meson 0.52.0 changed the default of the native: keyword (added in 0.48) so that no native: flag is equivalent to native:false. Projects that used add_project_arguments() without native: and expected it to apply to native targets now find flags missing from native compilations, causing undefined-reference / undeclared-identifier compile errors in native builds.

actions.hint: Use a Debian release with meson < 0.52.0 (e.g., Debian buster has meson 0.49)

non_solutions: Adding native: true to add_project_arguments calls is source modification and not allowed

summary: Config-tool based dependencies (llvm-config, cups-config, etc.) no longer search PATH during cross-compilation in meson >= 0.55.0, causing dependency not found errors.
mechanism: Projects cross-compiling that rely on config-tool dependencies (e.g., llvm-config) being found via PATH will fail at configure time because meson no longer searches PATH for these tools during cross builds; they must be specified in the cross file.

actions.hint: Use a Debian release with meson < 0.55.0 (e.g., Debian buster has meson 0.49)

non_solutions: Modifying the cross file is environment configuration but may not always be feasible without source changes

summary: The unstable-kconfig module was renamed to unstable-keyval in meson >= 0.55.0, causing import('unstable-kconfig') to fail.
mechanism: Old meson.build files using import('unstable-kconfig') will fail during meson setup because the module name no longer exists; it was renamed to unstable-keyval.

actions.hint: Use a Debian release with meson < 0.55.0 (e.g., Debian buster has meson 0.49)

non_solutions: Renaming the import in meson.build is source modification and not allowed

summary: Compiler.unittest_args() method was removed in Meson 0.60.0, causing a hard error if called in meson.build.
mechanism: The undocumented Compiler.unittest_args() method was fully removed after being deprecated; any meson.build that calls this method will fail with an unknown method error during meson setup.

actions.hint: Use an older Debian/environment with Meson < 0.60.0 to avoid this removal

non_solutions: Upgrading meson will not help since the method is permanently removed

summary: The Python module's dependency() method no longer accepts positional arguments in Meson 0.60.0, causing a hard error.
mechanism: Previously positional arguments to the Python module's dependency() method were ignored with a warning; in 0.60.0 they became a hard error, so meson.build files passing positional args to python.dependency() will fail during meson setup.

actions.hint: Use an older Debian/environment with Meson < 0.60.0 where positional arguments are silently ignored

non_solutions: Upgrading meson will not restore positional argument support

summary: CMake server API support was removed in Meson 0.62.0, breaking cmake subprojects that relied on CMake < 3.14.
mechanism: Meson dropped the deprecated CMake server API and now requires CMake >= 3.14 (File API) for cmake subprojects. Projects using cmake subprojects with an older CMake or relying on the server API path will fail during meson setup.

actions.hint: Use an older Debian/environment with Meson < 0.62.0 that still supports the CMake server API, or ensure CMake >= 3.14 is available

non_solutions: Downgrading CMake below 3.14 will not help since Meson no longer supports the server API path

summary: The JDK system dependency was renamed from 'jdk' to 'jni' in Meson 0.62.0, causing dependency('jdk') lookups to fail.
mechanism: Meson renamed the JDK system dependency identifier from 'jdk' to 'jni'. Any meson.build using dependency('jdk') will fail to find the dependency during meson setup because the name is no longer recognized.

actions.hint: Use an older Debian/environment with Meson < 0.62.0 where dependency('jdk') is still recognized

non_solutions: Installing JDK packages will not help since the dependency name itself changed in Meson

summary: Meson 1.7.0 no longer builds test targets as part of 'ninja all', causing test failures if test dependencies are not explicitly declared in meson.build.
mechanism: Previously 'meson test' invoked 'ninja all' unconditionally due to a bug, ensuring all test binaries were built. Now only explicitly declared test dependencies are built, so projects with missing build_by_default or undeclared test dependencies will fail when running tests.

actions.hint: Use 'ninja test' instead of 'ninja all && meson test', or run 'ninja all meson-test-prereq' before 'meson test --no-rebuild'
Use meson < 1.7.0 where test targets are still built by default

non_solutions: Adding --no-rebuild flag (makes the problem worse)
Running ninja all alone (no longer builds test targets)

summary: Meson treats unknown -D options as fatal, breaking packaging scripts that pass stale project options.
mechanism: Since Meson 0.60, unknown options are not only warnings. Old distro or CI build invocations can fail during meson setup/configure.

actions.hint: Remove the stale -D options from the meson setup command (unknown -D options are fatal since Meson 0.60)
Use Meson < 0.60 where unknown -D options were only a warning

summary: GCC 10 removed std::allocator members and disallows mismatched allocators in C++20
mechanism: Several members of std::allocator were removed for C++20 mode (use std::allocator_traits instead). The extension allowing containers with mismatched allocator types is no longer allowed even in -std=gnu++20 mode.

actions.hint: -std=c++17 or -std=gnu++17 to avoid C++20 allocator restrictions
Use GCC < 10

summary: GCC 11 in C++20 mode restricts operator>> for string extraction to arrays only
mechanism: When compiling as C++20, the operator>> overloads for extracting strings into character buffers only work with arrays, not raw pointers. Code passing char* to operator>> will fail to compile.
trigger_patterns: error: no matching function for call to 'operator>>'.*char\*

actions.hint: -std=c++17 to avoid C++20 operator>> restriction
Use GCC < 11

summary: GCC 12.3 made calling a std::bind result as volatile ill-formed for C++20 and later.
mechanism: Calling a std::bind result object qualified as volatile is ill-formed for C++20 and later. Code that invokes bind results through volatile references will fail to compile.
trigger_patterns: error: passing 'volatile std::_Bind<.*>' as 'this' argument discards qualifiers
error: no matching function for call to 'std::_Bind<.*>::operator\(\)<.*volatile

actions.hint: -std=c++17 or -std=gnu++17 (volatile std::bind calls are only ill-formed in C++20 and later)
Use GCC < 12.3 where volatile std::bind calls are still accepted

notes: Source only states 'Calling a std::bind result as volatile is ill-formed for C++20 and later'; no specific error text

summary: GCC 14 disallows std::basic_string with mismatched allocator type in C++20
mechanism: The extension allowing std::basic_string to be instantiated with an allocator that does not match the string's character type is no longer allowed in C++20 mode.

actions.hint: -std=c++17 to avoid C++20 string allocator restriction
Use GCC < 14

summary: GCC 3.4 changed allocator API, removed SGI-style allocator names, and renamed macro guard from _GLIBCPP_ to _GLIBCXX_
mechanism: Removed __simple_alloc, __allocator, __alloc, and _Alloc_traits. Changed default std::allocator from pool-based (__gnu_cxx::pool_allocator) to __gnu_cxx::new_allocator. Allocator extension headers moved to <ext/*.h>. Macro guard prefix changed from _GLIBCPP_ to _GLIBCXX_. Code using old allocator names or the old macro guard will fail to compile.
trigger_patterns: error: '(__simple_alloc|__allocator|__alloc|_Alloc_traits)' (was not declared|has not been declared|does not name a type)

actions.hint: Use -D_GLIBCXX_ macros instead of _GLIBCPP_ and update allocator usage to new names
Use GCC < 3.4

summary: GCC 4.3 removed legacy backward-compat headers and streamlined header dependencies
mechanism: Removed 30+ legacy headers (algobase.h, algo.h, alloc.h, bvector.h, complex.h, defalloc.h, deque.h, fstream.h, function.h, hash_map.h, hash_set.h, hashtable.h, heap.h, iomanip.h, iostream.h, istream.h, iterator.h, list.h, map.h, multimap.h, multiset.h, new.h, ostream.h, pair.h, queue.h, rope.h, set.h, slist.h, stack.h, streambuf.h, stream.h, tempbuf.h, tree.h, vector.h). Also <algorithm> no longer includes <climits>/<cstring>/<iosfwd>, <string> no longer includes <algorithm>/<memory>, etc.

actions.hint: Add explicit #include for required standard headers via -include flag
Use GCC < 4.3

summary: GCC 4.3 removed transitive header includes causing missing symbol errors
mechanism: <algorithm> no longer includes <climits>, <cstring>, or <iosfwd>. <bitset> no longer includes <istream>/<ostream>. <functional> no longer includes <cstddef>. <numeric> no longer includes <iterator>. <string> no longer includes <algorithm>/<memory>. <valarray> no longer includes <numeric>/<cstdlib>.
trigger_patterns: error: '(ptrdiff_t|size_t)' (does not name a type|was not declared)

actions.hint: Add -include <algorithm> or other missing headers
Use GCC < 4.3

summary: GCC 8 removed deprecated iostream members and copy_exception in C++17 mode
mechanism: ios_base::io_state, ios_base::open_mode, ios_base::seek_dir, basic_streambuf::stossc removed for C++17. std::copy_exception removed entirely. <complex.h> no longer includes C99 complex.h in C++11/14/17 modes.
trigger_patterns: error: '(io_state|open_mode|seek_dir)' in 'std::ios_base' (does not name a type|was not declared)
error: 'copy_exception' (is not a member of|was not declared)

actions.hint: -std=c++14 or -std=c++11 to avoid C++17 removals
Use GCC < 8

summary: GCC 8 disallows mismatched allocator types in containers in strict C++ modes
mechanism: The extension allowing containers to be instantiated with an allocator that does not match the container's value type is no longer allowed in strict -std=c++NN modes (only in -std=gnu++NN modes).
trigger_patterns: error: static assertion failed: .*allocator does not match.*value type
error: no type named 'allocator_type'.*does not match.*value_type

actions.hint: Use -std=gnu++17 instead of -std=c++17 to allow allocator extension
Use GCC < 8

summary: GCC 5 introduced dual ABI for std::string/std::list; mixing ABIs causes link failures
mechanism: GCC 5 moved std::string and std::list into std::__cxx11 namespace. Code compiled with different _GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI values cannot link together, producing undefined reference errors to std::__cxx11::* symbols.

actions.hint: -D_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI=0 to use old ABI
-D_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI=1 to use new ABI

non_solutions: Modifying source code to use different string types

summary: GCC 10 libstdc++ removed Profile Mode and __gnu_cxx::array_allocator.
mechanism: Old C++ code using libstdc++ profile extensions or array_allocator fails to compile or link with GCC 10+ libstdc++.
trigger_patterns: error:.*__gnu_cxx::array_allocator.*(not a member|undeclared|has not been declared)

actions.hint: Use GCC < 10 where __gnu_cxx::array_allocator and the <profile_container.h> Profile Mode are still available (both were fully removed in GCC 10, no flag restores them)

summary: Bison 2.5 no longer appends semicolons to user actions ending with cpp directives or braced compound initializers
mechanism: Previously Bison appended a semicolon to every user action for reductions. Starting with 2.5, actions ending with a cpp directive or braced compound initializer no longer get an automatic semicolon appended, causing C compiler errors about missing semicolons in the generated parser.

actions.hint: Add missing semicolons after actions in .y grammar file that end with cpp directives
Use bison < 2.5

non_solutions: Editing generated parser C files directly (they get regenerated)

summary: Bison 2.6 removed YYTOKEN_TABLE and YYERROR_VERBOSE from C++ generated headers
mechanism: The symbols YYTOKEN_TABLE and YYERROR_VERBOSE were removed from C++ generated headers to allow multiple parser headers in one compilation unit. Code checking #ifdef YYTOKEN_TABLE or YYERROR_VERBOSE in C++ parsers will behave differently.

actions.hint: -DYYTOKEN_TABLE=1 or -DYYERROR_VERBOSE=1 if needed
Use bison < 2.6

non_solutions: Defining the macros manually in user code re-introduces the multiple-parser-header collision that 2.6 fixed.

summary: Bison 3.0 removed YYFAIL support; generated parsers using it fail to compile
mechanism: Support for YYFAIL was removed (deprecated since 2.4.2). Grammar files using YYFAIL will generate code that fails to compile because the macro is no longer defined in the parser skeleton.

actions.hint: Edit the .y grammar file to replace YYFAIL with YYERROR (or `yyerror(...); return 1;` for non-recovering parsers).
Regenerate the parser with bison < 3.0 (or pass -DYYFAIL=YYERROR via CPPFLAGS as a transitional shim).
Use bison < 3.0 to keep emitting YYFAIL.

non_solutions: Editing generated parser C files directly (they get regenerated)

summary: Bison 3.0 removed YYLEX_PARAM and YYPARSE_PARAM support
mechanism: Support for YYLEX_PARAM and YYPARSE_PARAM macros was removed (deprecated since 1.875). Grammars using these will generate parsers that fail to compile. Use %lex-param, %parse-param, or %param instead.

actions.hint: In the .y grammar file, migrate YYLEX_PARAM/YYPARSE_PARAM to the %lex-param, %parse-param, or %param directives.
As a shim, pass -DYYLEX_PARAM=<lexarg> -DYYPARSE_PARAM=<parsearg> via CPPFLAGS.
Use bison < 3.0 (deprecated since 1.875).

non_solutions: Editing generated parser files

summary: Bison 3.0 removed lowercase yystype/yyltype support
mechanism: Support for lowercase yystype and yyltype was removed (deprecated since 1.875). Code must use uppercase YYSTYPE and YYLTYPE.

actions.hint: Replace lowercase yystype/yyltype references in user code and grammar prologue with uppercase YYSTYPE/YYLTYPE.
Use bison < 3.0 (deprecated since 1.875).

summary: Bison 3.5 changed C++ position line/column types from unsigned to int
mechanism: In C++ parsers, line numbers and columns are now represented as 'int' not 'unsigned'. Code that assigns or compares position members with unsigned types may get sign-comparison warnings or errors with -Werror.

actions.hint: Pass -Wno-sign-compare (and -Wno-narrowing if needed) for the generated C++ parser translation units.
Update user code that compares position.line()/column() against unsigned types to use the new counter_type (int) typedef.
Use bison < 3.5 to keep the unsigned line/column representation.

summary: Bison 3.8 in Yacc mode generates yyerror/yylex prototypes that conflict with user declarations
mechanism: In Yacc compatibility mode (-y/--yacc), Bison 3.8 generates prototypes for yyerror and yylex. If user code already declares these functions differently (static, specific attributes, different signatures), the generated parser fails to compile. Note: Bison 3.8.1 restricted this to only when POSIXLY_CORRECT is set.

actions.hint: Add -Wno-yacc (or set YACC='bison -o y.tab.c' instead of 'bison -y') so 3.8 does not emit yyerror/yylex prototypes.
Insert `#define yyerror yyerror` and `#define yylex yylex` before #including the generated parser header, so Bison's prototype is suppressed.
Use bison 3.8.1+ (the prototype emission was restricted to POSIXLY_CORRECT), or bison < 3.8.

summary: Bison 3.8 removed YYPRINT macro support
mechanism: Support for the YYPRINT macro was removed. It only worked with yacc.c and only for tokens. Code defining YYPRINT will get compile errors or unused-macro warnings.

actions.hint: Remove the YYPRINT macro from the .y grammar file and migrate its body to a %printer directive (works for any skeleton, not only yacc.c).
Use bison < 3.8 (YYPRINT was deprecated since 1.50 / removed in 3.8).

summary: Bison deprecated directives and C++ parser class variable changes can become hard errors under -Werror or duplicate definitions.
mechanism: Bison 3.3 emits replacement diagnostics for old directives such as %error-verbose and parser_class_name; mixed old/new declarations can produce redefinition errors.

actions.hint: Use %define parse.error verbose and %define api.parser.class consistently; remove duplicate old parser_class_name definitions.

summary: Bison dangling string aliases can fail parser generation when warnings are errors.
mechanism: Bison introduced diagnostics for string literals not attached to grammar symbols. Projects enabling -Werror can fail during generated parser creation.
trigger_patterns: string literal.*not attached to a symbol

actions.hint: Declare the string as a %token alias or remove the dangling literal from %type/%nterm declarations.

summary: Bison conflict expectation mismatches stop parser generation with explicit conflict-count errors.
mechanism: Since Bison 3.0, conflict reporting was normalized: when %expect or %expect-rr is set, an unexpected conflict count is a hard error ("shift/reduce conflicts: N found, M expected" / reduce/reduce), and -Werror=conflicts-sr/-Werror=conflicts-rr turn ordinary conflicts into errors. Projects with stale %expect/%expect-rr values therefore fail parser generation under newer Bison.

actions.hint: Fix the grammar or update %expect/%expect-rr to the current conflict count after review.

summary: Specifying -allow-undefined to libtool link mode is now a fatal error instead of being silently accepted
mechanism: In libtool 1.9b (first stable release: 2.2), the -allow-undefined link mode option was changed from accepted to a fatal error. Old projects that pass -allow-undefined in their Makefile.am LDFLAGS or libtool link invocations will fail at link time when built with libtool >= 2.2.

actions.hint: Remove -allow-undefined from LDFLAGS, _LDFLAGS, or libtool link invocations in Makefile.am or configure.ac
Use older Debian with libtool < 1.9b (i.e. libtool 1.5.x)

non_solutions: Adding -allow-undefined back is not possible since the option is rejected by the tool

summary: Libtool no longer infers the operation mode from command arguments; --mode must be specified explicitly
mechanism: In libtool 1.9b (first stable release: 2.2), mode inference was removed. Previously libtool could guess whether it was in compile, link, or install mode from the arguments. Now --mode=compile, --mode=link, etc. must be passed explicitly. Projects with hand-written libtool invocations that relied on mode inference will fail.

actions.hint: Add explicit --mode=compile or --mode=link to libtool invocations in Makefile.am or custom build scripts
